question: Why is the magnetic polaron formation time shorter than the circular polarization evolution time scale in type-II Zn,MnTe/ZnSe quantum dots under a magnetic field?
answer: In type-II Zn,MnTe/ZnSe quantum dots under a magnetic field, magnetic polaron formation occurs faster than the evolution of photoluminescence circular polarization.  This observation stems from time-resolved photoluminescence studies comparing magnetic and non-magnetic samples, revealing a significant difference in the time scales of these two processes.

The paper aims to investigate the dynamics of magnetic polarons in type-II (Zn,Mn)Te/ZnSe quantum dots under an external magnetic field using time-resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy. Specifically, the study focuses on the time evolution of circularly polarized photoluminescence components and circular polarization of emitted light. It explores the system's behavior, including the differing time scales for magnetic polaron formation and photoluminescence circular polarization evolution, and discusses the findings within a theoretical framework related to magnetic susceptibility as a function of temperature.
